provider_policy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundary_decision.rationale: Two independent axes are in play. The frozen registry's record_plane is 'world-model,' a catalog-shelving classification describing where WM-XCT-031 sits within Vercy's world-model corpus; it says nothing about the subject model's own ontological shape and must never be substituted for entry_kind. On the entry_kind axis, 'mixin' is the most defensible schema-enum value: the scope_statement opens by declaring 'WM-XCT-031 is a mixin that attaches linguistic and locale context to a host record,' reinforced by seven separate inline_only_rationale clauses and the binding-lifecycle finding's explicit 'host-dependent weak identity, keyed by host object reference plus target field or resource path plus monotonic binding version.' Alternatives were considered and rejected: 'entity' fails because no independent aggregate root is asserted anywhere in the evidence; 'relationship' was considered because a 'binding' is literally an association between a host and a locale declaration, but the model carries far more attribute payload, lifecycle and governance machinery than a pure join construct, and its own authors chose mixin language throughout. This matches the frozen registry's existing entry_kind value, so no reclassification is required. That said, the full lifecycle/roles/access/retention service scaffolding built around this 'mixin,' together with two artifacts (locale profile release, stewardship charter) whose identity is issued by an external profile-owning or governance body and is reusable across many bindings rather than scoped to one host, mean the record's own 'boundary-review-required' review_state is warranted and should remain open rather than being cleared by this audit.

decisions.concept: Entry kind classification (mixin) vs. record-plane classification (world-model)
decisions.disposition: Accepted — mixin confirmed as the defensible subject-model entry kind; world-model record_plane is a separate, non-conflicting registry-shelving axis.
decisions.rationale: The scope_statement, seven inline_only_rationale clauses, and host-dependent weak-identity design (host reference plus field/path plus version) repeatedly assert mixin semantics with no independent root entity, event or relationship type proposed anywhere in the evidence.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity strategy across all 16 serial artifacts
decisions.rationale: Every serial artifact's identity_strategy follows the declared three-tier priority (master-system id, then governed IRI, then UUID/ULID) and none uses a date, tag, or version label as the sole key, matching artifact_rules.identity_priority and the timestamp_rule exactly.

decisions.concept: Locale profile release and stewardship charter artifacts reading as cross-host reusable entities
decisions.disposition: Deferred — kept inline as artifacts of this mixin for now, flagged for future extraction review.
decisions.rationale: Their identity is issued by an external profile-owning or governance body and is designed to be referenced by many bindings across many hosts, which is closer to a shared registry entity than a per-binding by-product, and no relationship-contract entry exists yet to test this against sibling models.

decisions.concept: Model name 'Localization / Language' versus actual scope weight toward translation and terminology
decisions.disposition: Deferred — name retained as-is, scope-split evaluation recommended for a future pass.
decisions.rationale: Three of seven bundles (translatable-unit binding, message-form/fallback contracts, terminology/quality assertions) address translation-workflow binding rather than pure locale/language identity, so the name may undersell roughly forty percent of the modeled surface.

decisions.concept: Composition relations (REFERENCE, EXTEND, ALIGN) asserted in prose versus the frozen empty relationship-contract
decisions.disposition: Accepted as an expected sequencing gap, not a defect.
decisions.rationale: boundary_notes and adversarial_checks name specific link types to seven neighbor model families, but relationship-contract is empty and parent_ids/contains_ids/aligned_model_ids are blank in the frozen registry record, consistent with a candidate-status record awaiting registry-wide population rather than a contradiction.

decisions.concept: Full lifecycle, roles, access and retention service-layer scaffolding attached to entry_kind mixin
decisions.rationale: Approval, supersession, disclosure and disposition machinery normally associated with aggregate or entity roots is fully specified here for a binding that otherwise claims only host-dependent weak identity, and this cannot be checked against other Vercy mixins without tool access.

decisions.concept: Retention and deletion posture (tombstone, hold-blocking, delegated execution)
decisions.disposition: Accepted, with the self-declared 'gap' rating carried forward as a publication hold rather than treated as blocking.
decisions.rationale: The disposition, hold, and tombstone rules are internally consistent with the correction-by-supersession and declaration-is-not-enforcement policies, but rest on a single national archives authority's requirements because ISO 15489-1 could not be retrieved, which the checklist itself already labels a gap.

decisions.concept: Access and disclosure design (deny-by-default, bundle/layer/finding/artifact scopes, break-glass)
decisions.rationale: The six declared exceptions, the deny-by-default default rule, and the explicit statement that evaluation and enforcement are external are mutually consistent with the model's repeated declaration-is-not-enforcement policy and with the disclosure profile artifact's own scope grains.

decisions.concept: Naming disambiguation among loc-locale-fn-resolve-declared-preferences, loc-gov-resolve-locale-fn and loc-trans-fn-resolve-fallback
decisions.disposition: Accepted with a naming-clarity note, not blocking.
decisions.rationale: Each function operates on a different object (inventory, host-object bindings, and fallback-chain profile respectively) and is not a true duplicate, but the shared 'resolve' verb without disambiguating qualifiers risks implementer confusion and should be tightened in a future revision.

decisions.concept: Source currency for sources dated or accessed on the audit's own generation date (2026-09-03), including the SRC-010 HTML Living Standard
decisions.disposition: Deferred to a live-verification publication hold.
decisions.rationale: A Living Standard and several registry or code-list pages carry access or revision dates identical to this pass's generated_at timestamp, which this no-tools audit cannot re-verify, so currency must be confirmed before the draft is treated as source-verified rather than merely source-cited.

deferred_research: Evaluate whether the locale profile release and stewardship charter artifacts should become standalone registry-type Vercy models once real multi-Dimension reuse evidence exists, rather than remaining artifacts nested inside this mixin.

Retrieve ISO 15489-1 and at least one applicable data-protection statute to close the self-declared retention-and-deletion and privacy gaps, replacing the current single-anchor NARA-only retention basis.
Determine whether Vercy already defines or should define a generic cross-cutting role/authority-assignment pattern, and check the six localization-specific roles here for duplication against it.

Confirm against other registered Vercy mixins whether full lifecycle, approval, supersession, disclosure and disposition service machinery is the established pattern for entry_kind mixin, to keep cross-registry consistency.

Research a cross-engine machine-translation confidence calibration reference and a translation-supply-chain security threat model, both explicitly flagged as gaps with no primary source located in this pass.
publication_holds: Live re-verification is required for all 32 cited sources before publication, especially the SRC-010 HTML Living Standard and the SRC-003/SRC-013/SRC-028/SRC-029 registry and code-list pages whose accessed-or-revision dates coincide with this pass's own generation timestamp of 2026-09-03, since this no-tools audit cannot browse to confirm current validity.

This draft carries a visible, owner-authorized single-provider hold: Grok was waived from the WM-XCT-031 research queue by the repository owner on 2026-08-29 after repeated structured-output failures, so the record must be published as a reviewable draft pending independent second-provider or human domain-expert review, not as a cross-validated result.

The self-declared checklist gaps for retention-and-deletion, privacy, security and negotiation determinism rest on a single national-archives anchor and no retrieved data-protection or ISO 15489-1 text; these must be resolved or explicitly carried as caveats in any downstream policy built on this model.

The relationship-contract for WM-XCT-031 is currently empty while boundary_notes and adversarial_checks name specific REFERENCE, EXTEND and ALIGN links to seven neighbor model families; these should be reconciled into registered composition links before this record is treated as fully positioned in the Vercy graph.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
